name: Sideconvo
author: Sideconvo

sections.description:
Sideconvo integrates AI-powered semantic search into your WordPress site by syncing your content to a vector database. Enable your visitors to find relevant information quickly using natural language queries.

Key Features

  • Seamless integration with Sideconvo platform
  • Automatic content synchronization
  • Support for posts, pages, and custom post types
  • Taxonomy syncing (categories, tags, custom taxonomies)
  • Selective content indexing with exclusions
  • Real-time sync status monitoring
  • Environment-based configuration (dev, qa, prod)
  • Memory-optimized batch processing
  • Automatic expiration and reconciliation

How It Works

  1. Connect your WordPress site to Sideconvo using your API key
  2. Select which content types to sync (posts, pages, custom post types, taxonomies)
  3. Initial indexing runs automatically
  4. Ongoing changes sync in real-time
  5. Your content becomes searchable via Sideconvo’s AI

Requirements

  • PHP 7.4 or higher
  • WordPress 6.0 or higher
  • Sideconvo account and API key

External Services

Important: This plugin connects to external Sideconvo services to provide AI-powered content indexing and search functionality.

This plugin integrates with Sideconvo (https://www.sideconvo.ai), a third-party AI platform that indexes your WordPress content and makes it searchable via natural language queries.

When does the connection occur?

The plugin communicates with Sideconvo’s API in the following situations:

  • When you authenticate using your API key during initial setup
  • When content is published, updated, or deleted on your WordPress site
  • When the reconciliation tool runs to compare local and remote sync state
  • When bulk sync or remove actions are triggered from the WP admin list tables
  • When the scheduled WP-Cron task checks for expired content

No data is transmitted until you connect your site with a valid Sideconvo API key.

What data is transmitted?

When the plugin syncs content to Sideconvo, the following data is sent to Sideconvo’s servers:

  • Post or term ID (used as the unique record identifier)
  • Post or term title
  • Post or term URL
  • Post or term body content (HTML)
  • Featured image URL
  • Last modified timestamp
  • Your site’s namespace (derived from your API key)

Data Processing

All content indexing and AI search processing is handled on Sideconvo’s servers. Sideconvo uses this data to:

  • Index your content in a vector database for semantic search
  • Respond to natural language queries from your site visitors
  • Maintain sync state between your WordPress site and the platform

Privacy & Terms

For more information about how Sideconvo handles your data, please review:

  • Sideconvo Privacy Policy: https://www.sideconvo.ai/privacy/
  • Sideconvo Terms of Service: https://www.sideconvo.ai/terms

Your Responsibilities

As a site owner using this plugin, you are responsible for:

  • Informing your visitors that your site content is indexed by Sideconvo’s AI platform
  • Including Sideconvo’s privacy policy information in your site’s privacy documentation
  • Obtaining necessary user consent per applicable privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, etc.)
  • Understanding Sideconvo’s data handling practices
  • Ensuring compliance with your local data protection laws

Service Provider

This external service is provided by:

Sideconvo AI

  • Website: https://www.sideconvo.ai
  • API: https://api.sideconvo.ai
  • Service: AI-powered content indexing and semantic search platform

Stripe

The Sideconvo platform, which is loaded via an iframe inside the plugin’s admin interface, uses Stripe for payment processing. Stripe JavaScript is loaded within that iframe context to handle billing for Sideconvo subscriptions.

No payment data is collected or transmitted by this WordPress plugin directly — all Stripe interactions occur entirely within the Sideconvo platform iframe.

This service is provided by Stripe, Inc.:

  • Terms of Service: https://stripe.com/legal/ssa
  • Privacy Policy: https://stripe.com/privacy

Source Code

The JavaScript and CSS assets in this plugin are compiled from TypeScript/React source code using @wordpress/scripts (webpack + Babel).

The full source code is available on Bitbucket.

Build Requirements

  • Node.js 18+
  • npm 8+

Build Instructions

  1. Clone the repository
  2. Install dependencies: npm install
  3. Build for production: npm run build
  4. Build for development (with watch): npm run start
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/sideconvo/, or install through the WordPress plugins screen
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress
  3. Navigate to the ‘Sideconvo’ menu in wp-admin
  4. Click ‘Connect to Sideconvo’ to authenticate with your API key
  5. Select the content types you want to sync
  6. Wait for initial indexing to complete
sections.faq:
Do I need a Sideconvo account?

Yes, you’ll need to sign up at https://platform.sideconvo.ai/ to get your API key.

What content can I sync?

You can sync posts, pages, custom post types, and taxonomies (categories, tags, custom taxonomies).

Can I exclude specific content from syncing?

Yes, you can exclude individual items or use the metabox on edit screens to control sync settings.

How much does Sideconvo cost?

Pricing information is available at https://www.sideconvo.ai/pricing

Is my data secure?

Yes, all communication with Sideconvo uses encrypted HTTPS connections. Your API key is stored securely in WordPress options.

How do I enable debug logging?

Add the following line to your wp-config.php:

define( 'SIDECONVO_DEBUG_LOG', true );

When enabled, the plugin writes diagnostic entries to your PHP error log (subject to WordPress’s WP_DEBUG_LOG setting). This includes details about reconciliation scans, Pinecone list fetches, and orphaned-document delete operations. Leave this undefined or set to false on production sites.

What happens if I deactivate the plugin?

Your sync data is preserved. Reactivating the plugin will resume syncing from where it left off.

What happens if I uninstall the plugin?

All plugin data including sync state and settings will be permanently deleted from WordPress. Your content remains in Sideconvo’s database.
sections.changelog:
1.3.3

  • Removed background WP-Cron job (sideconvo_background_sync) — sync is now driven exclusively by the frontend polling loop
  • Removed stale legacy cron cleanup entries from uninstall for hooks that were never actively scheduled
  • Added activation-path cleanup to remove any lingering sideconvo_background_sync cron event left over from plugin upgrades without deactivation

1.3.2

  • Increased Sideconvo search API timeout from 5 to 15 seconds to prevent intermittent MySQL fallback caused by latency spikes

1.3.1

  • Fixed duplicate category/tag cards on multilingual sites (WPML, Polylang): Term_Query_Interceptor now filters matched terms to the current page language before returning them to the theme
  • Fixed cross-language post leakage via term expansion: posts resolved from term_* API results are now filtered by current language alongside direct post ID hits

1.3.0

  • Added AI-powered semantic search integration: WordPress search queries are intercepted and routed to Sideconvo’s vector search backend, returning results ranked by relevance
  • Added two-layer search cache (WP object cache + transients) with configurable TTL to minimise API calls and reduce latency
  • Added Search Term Expander: term_* IDs returned by the vector search are automatically resolved to their associated post IDs before WordPress renders the results
  • Added graceful MySQL fallback: if the Sideconvo search API is unavailable, WordPress falls back to its native search without any disruption
  • Added Search Integration card to the Settings screen with enable/disable toggle, cache TTL input, debug-logging toggle, and a live connection status pill
  • Added Search quick-toggle to the sidebar, mirroring the Widget Visibility toggle for fast on/off access
  • Added search diagnostics REST endpoint (sideconvo/v1/search/status) for verifying connectivity from wp-admin
  • Added automatic search cache invalidation after any post or taxonomy sync or delete operation

1.2.0

  • Added language filtering support for WPML and Polylang: excluded-language items are filtered from scope, batch processing, reconciliation counts, and the Sync table
  • Added Languages section to Content Types settings with per-language item counts and delete confirmation modal
  • Added global disconnect state: api_key_status option surfaces an admin notice and reconnect link when the API key becomes invalid
  • Added DisconnectBanner on the Sync screen with reconnect link and stale-lag indicator
  • Added Run Sync button to the Sync screen for manual on-demand re-index
  • Added no-scope empty state on the Sync screen when no content types are selected
  • Added three-state inline notices on the Sync screen (success, info, error)
  • Added Presentations menu item under PDFs & Knowledge in the sidebar
  • Added Logger::error() and Logger::warning() methods for always-on production error visibility (not gated by SIDECONVO_DEBUG_LOG)
  • Added PHP debug logging around the pinecone/list reconciliation fetch phase
  • Added content hash change detection for taxonomy terms to trigger re-sync on description/name edits
  • Added sideconvo_content_hash_fields filter for extensible per-post-type content hashing
  • Added auto-delete of orphaned Pinecone items when scope drops to zero
  • Added domain migration re-index: all content is automatically re-synced when siteurl or home URL changes
  • Upgraded database schema to v2: dual timestamps (last_sync_local / last_sync_cloud), pending_delete intent flag, and a STORED GENERATED derived status column
  • Upgraded batch processor to 4-phase architecture with SKIP LOCKED and advisory lock fallback for concurrent-safe queue processing
  • Upgraded sidebar status card to show a live health dot and hover popover (Sync Health + Needs Attention) with direct navigation links to filtered Sync screen views
  • Fixed Sync All re-indexing the entire content set after a scope change instead of only newly added items
  • Fixed first-run auto-sync triggering incorrectly after a scope change when items were already indexed
  • Fixed orphaned items not being auto-deleted after scope changes
  • Fixed queue-missing phase re-queuing already-indexed items during Pinecone async lag, causing an infinite progress loop
  • Fixed reconciliation filtering out URL-shaped IDs from the Pinecone list response
  • Fixed sync table rows not being removed when a post type is removed from the content types selection
  • Fixed tombstone rows incorrectly included in domain-change reset (Sync_State::reset_all)
  • Fixed Sync_State::upsert() coercing null datetime fields to empty strings
  • Fixed HTTP 500 body from Sideconvo cloud functions now logged at error level (was debug-only)
  • Fixed deletionSucceeded flag: setReconciliationReport(orphaned: 0) now only runs when the delete batch completes without throwing
  • Fixed WPML: Sync page table showing 0 items when multiple languages are active
  • Fixed Polylang: term language SQL for REST context self-heal
  • Fixed language-excluded categories and tags still counted as indexed in stats
  • Fixed indexed > scope display bug in the sidebar status popover
  • Fixed button spinner showing during reconciliation; banner is now the sole loading indicator
  • Fixed Pages in Scope and Pages Indexed status cards incorrectly shown when counts are equal
  • Fixed warning notification now shown when auto-delete of orphaned items fails mid-run
  • Removed dead allSyncedBanner CSS classes

1.1.1

  • Fixed reconciliation polling looping when rate-limited: retry cap raised to cover the full 429 Retry-After window
  • Fixed “Pages Indexed” count mismatch between sidebar and Sync screen during active reconciliation
  • Fixed items incorrectly showing as “Missing” after a content-types sync due to stale recentlySyncedIdsRef
  • Fixed all items showing as “Missing” after a fresh sync during Pinecone’s async catch-up window
  • Fixed site-disabled banner not surfacing on first detection when sync was blocked with a 503
  • Fixed persistent orphaned taxonomy terms accumulating after repeated add/remove cycles
  • Improved site-disabled detection: replaced fragile regex matching with a machine-readable error_code field
  • Improved rate-limit status message: removed “(waiting for rate limit to clear)” suffix for consistency

1.1.0

  • Fixed Conversations sub-menu items (Conversations, Highlights, Users) missing icons in the sidebar
  • Added detection of site_disabled error with admin warning banner linking to the subscriptions page for reactivation
  • Added Pinecone list endpoint pagination support via X-Next-Token for large indexes
  • Added Sideconvo logo SVG to the wp-admin menu, replacing the generic dashicons-cloud icon
  • Disabled all sync operations (upsert, delete, list) when the site subscription is inactive
  • Improved auth/site-status checking: removed per-second polling; now re-checks only on plugin open or on 403
  • Improved sidebar layout and visual polish

1.0.0

  • Fixed HTTP 429 rate-limit handling: sync queue now pauses for the exact Retry-After duration and resumes automatically without user interaction
  • Fixed batch sync items failing silently with progress banner stuck at “0 of N items processed”
  • Fixed stale “Pages Indexed” count on Sync screen after all WordPress content is removed
  • Fixed race condition in delete batch lock using atomic add_option() DB mutex (TOCTOU-safe)
  • Fixed stale PHP-localized scope count triggering unwanted auto-indexing when all content types are removed in the same page session
  • Fixed out-of-scope posts and taxonomy terms being re-synced after removal from scope
  • Fixed unpublished/deleted posts being marked as failed instead of excluded during batch processing
  • Improved sync progress banner: now shows items attempted (not just successfully indexed) and surfaces failed count inline
  • Improved batch retry logic: server_broken early-abort prevents hammering the API when server is systematically failing
  • Improved reconciliation: auto-triggers when scope drops to zero to surface orphaned Pinecone items
  • Removed forced navigation guard (SyncGuard) that blocked access to dashboard routes before initial sync

0.8.1

  • Added CSRF nonce protection to widget params handler (handle_widget_params)
  • Added Source Code section to readme.txt with build instructions

0.8.0

  • Fixed broken privacy policy URL in readme.txt
  • Added HTTP 429 rate-limit handling with backoff and retry logic
  • Added configurable sync delay setting (0 = immediate dispatch, >0 = deferred)
  • Improved save_post hook debouncing to prevent duplicate API calls on publish
  • Improved delayed queue dispatch after publish to reduce API fatigue
  • Improved API key security: lazy-loaded on reveal/copy only, no logging or accidental exposure, key rotation support
  • Replaced echo style tag with wp_add_inline_style() per WordPress coding standards
  • Scoped list-table CSS to admin post screens only to prevent style leakage
  • Documented Stripe as an external service in readme.txt
  • Removed background sync toggle and WP-Cron batch runner

0.7.0

  • Fixed encoding issues with special characters in post titles and content
  • Fixed reconciliation not catching orphaned records after re-connection
  • Improved add/remove content type sync flow with better bulk remove handling
  • Improved overall admin experience and error messaging

0.6.0

  • Fixed Sync All looping infinitely when no content types are in scope
  • Fixed title encoding for posts containing HTML entities
  • Fixed sync and expiration logic edge cases
  • Added “Expired” filter to WP List Tables for easier content management
  • Improved unsync/sync behaviour when content types are added or removed
  • Stability improvements for batch delete operations

0.5.0

  • Initial public release
  • Plugin scaffold with PSR-4 autoloading and React admin interface
  • Environment configuration system (dev/qa/prod)
  • Sideconvo platform authentication via iframe login flow
  • Site configuration wizard with content type and taxonomy selection
  • Batch indexing with memory-optimised batch sizing (128MB/512MB thresholds)
  • Post-wizard app shell with left navigation and platform iframes
  • Metabox on post and term edit screens with per-item sync controls
  • Expiration date support for time-limited content indexing
  • Automatic sync hooks on post save, status transition, and deletion
  • Taxonomy sync fields mirroring the post metabox UI
  • WP List Table enhancements: bulk Sync/Remove actions and sync status filter
  • Custom sync status column on post and taxonomy list screens
  • Reconciliation engine comparing WordPress and Sideconvo state
  • Admin notices summarising bulk action results
  • WP-Cron scheduled expiration checks
  • Full i18n support with sideconvo text domain
  • Security hardening: nonces, capability checks, input sanitisation, output escaping

Introduces WPML/Polylang language filtering, database schema v2, a 4-phase batch processor, domain migration auto-re-index, and a redesigned sidebar health popover. Includes numerous sync reliability and reconciliation fixes. A database migration runs automatically on first activation.
upgrade_notice.1.1.1: Bug fix release. Resolves orphaned taxonomy term accumulation, Missing count false-positives after sync, mismatched Pages Indexed counts, site-disabled banner not surfacing on first detection, and 429 reconciliation retry loops.
upgrade_notice.1.1.0: Recommended update. Adds subscription-aware sync gating with admin warning, Pinecone list pagination for large indexes, and fixes for transient network errors, sidebar count mismatches, and reconciliation cache invalidation when syncing individual missing items.
upgrade_notice.1.0.0: Recommended update. Resolves rate-limit handling, silent batch failures, stale sync counts, and a delete lock race condition. Improves sync progress feedback and reconciliation accuracy.
upgrade_notice.0.8.1: WordPress.org compliance update. Fixes CSRF vulnerability in widget params handler, corrects privacy policy URL, includes plugin source code, and documents all external services.
upgrade_notice.0.8.0: Recommended update. Includes rate-limit handling, API key security hardening, WordPress.org compliance improvements, and simplification of sync behaviour (fixed 5-second delay, background sync removed).
upgrade_notice.0.7.0: Recommended update. Fixes sync reliability issues, encoding problems, and improves the content type add/remove flow.
upgrade_notice.0.6.0: Bug fix release. Resolves infinite sync loop, title encoding issues, and improves expiration handling.
